---
title: "13 Research the dissemination and implementation of methods"
link-citations: true
---
Alternative labels: methodological implementation science

## Definition
These studies aim to understand or improve the dissemination, implementation, or de-implementation of methods in health research practice. They assess current implementation, identify barriers and facilitators, develop dissemination or implementation strategies, or test the effectiveness of such strategies.

This type of methods research is still rare. Examples come mostly from areas of reporting guidelines and core outcome sets. Different approaches are possible:

## Typical approaches and corresponding examples 
[Quantitative survey](../approaches/6survey.qmd): Survey of researchers to identify barriers to the implementation of new statistical methods.[@Pullenayegum2016knowledge]

[Qualitative study involving researchers or other interest-holders in health research](../approaches/7qualitative.qmd): interviews with trial investigators to understand why they did not use existing core outcome sets;[@Hughes2022in-depth] survey of investigators in sports medicine to understand why they did not use a specific reporting guideline.[@Hansford2024barriers]

[Review of applied methods](../approaches/9review-applied.qmd): proportion of trials using core outcome sets.[@Matvienko-Sikar2022use]

## Guidance
The only paper that explicitly addresses methodological implementation science that we know is King 2019.[@King2019using]
